problem: Find the equation of the right-opening parabola that has its vertex at $(-4,-3)$ and passes through the point $(1,2).$
worked_solution:
The general standard equation of a parabola whose vertex is $(h,k)$ and whose arms open right or left is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}(y-k)^{2} & =4p(x-h).\end{aligned}
$$

Since we know that the given parabola has its vertex at $(h,k)=(-4,-3),$ we substitute $h=-4$ and $k=-3$ into the equation above and get

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =4p(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$

We also know that the given parabola passes through the point $(1,2),$ so we can substitute $x=1$ and $y=2$ into the equation above and solve for $p:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =4p(x+4) \\ (2+3)^{2} & =4p(1+4) \\ 25 & =20p \\ p & =\frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

So, the equation of the parabola is 

$$
\begin{aligned}(y+3)^{2} & =4p(x+4) \\ (y+3)^{2} & =4(\frac{5}{4})(x+4) \\ (y+3)^{2} & =5(x+4).\end{aligned}
$$
